# Mustache Template Guide

Email and SMS templates use **Mustache**, a logic-less templating language. Variables are inserted with double curly braces: `{{variableName}}`.

## Basic Interpolation

```html
<p>Your verification code is: <strong>{{code}}</strong></p>
<p>Welcome to {{appName}}!</p>
```

Values are HTML-escaped by default. Use triple braces `{{{var}}}` to render raw HTML.

---

## Built-in Variables

Always available when a code is sent:

| Variable | Description |
| -------- | ----------- |
| `code`   | The one-time verification code |

---

## Project Data Variables

Populated from your project's **Custom Data** settings:

| Variable       | Description                                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `appName`      | Application display name                          |
| `companyName`  | Company name — also used as the email sender name |
| `supportEmail` | Support contact address                           |
| `websiteUrl`   | Your website URL                                  |
| `logoUrl`      | URL to your logo image                            |
| `primaryColor` | Brand color (e.g. `#4F46E5`)                      |
| `emailFrom`    | Override the sender email address                 |

Any **custom key-value pairs** added to project data are also available as template variables.

---

## Sections — Conditionals & Loops

Wrap content in `{{#variable}}...{{/variable}}` to render it only when the value is truthy:

```html
{{#supportEmail}}
  <p>Questions? <a href="mailto:{{supportEmail}}">{{supportEmail}}</a></p>
{{/supportEmail}}
```

Sections also iterate over arrays — each item's properties become available inside:

```html
{{#items}}
  <li>{{name}}</li>
{{/items}}
```

---

## Inverted Sections — Fallbacks

Use `{{^variable}}...{{/variable}}` to render content when a value is **falsy or absent**:

```html
{{^companyName}}
  <p>Your verification code</p>
{{/companyName}}
{{#companyName}}
  <p>{{companyName}} verification code</p>
{{/companyName}}
```

---

## Custom Function Values

For advanced dynamic values, store a **JavaScript function body** in any project data field by prefixing it with `function::`.

### Format

```
function::return props.companyName ? props.companyName.toUpperCase() : "ACME";
```

The function receives a `props` argument containing all other template variables, letting you compute derived values at send time.

### Example

Set project data:

| Key        | Value                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `greeting` | `function::return "Hello from " + (props.companyName || "us") + "!";` |

Use in template:

```html
<p>{{greeting}}</p>
<!-- Renders: Hello from Acme! -->
```

### Use Cases

- **Dynamic subjects**: derive a value from multiple fields
- **Formatted values**: uppercase, truncate, or format a variable
- **Conditional text**: return different strings based on other fields

> **Note:** Functions run server-side. Only project administrators can set project data values.

---

## Full Example

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
  {{#logoUrl}}
  <img src="{{logoUrl}}" alt="{{appName}}" style="height:40px" />
  {{/logoUrl}}

  <h2>Your verification code</h2>

  <div style="font-size:32px; letter-spacing:8px; font-weight:bold;">
    {{code}}
  </div>

  <p>This code expires in 10 minutes.</p>

  {{#supportEmail}}
  <p>Need help? <a href="mailto:{{supportEmail}}">Contact support</a></p>
  {{/supportEmail}}

  <footer>
    &copy; 2026 {{companyName}}
  </footer>
</body>
</html>
```
